name: Question 11
problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $x=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Given that the point $P(\frac{\pi }{2},1,0)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{y}=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}y)$, which of the following gives a tangent vector to $C$ at $P?$
worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface with the plane $x=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point $P$ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{y}(\frac{\pi }{2},1).$ 

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ at $(\frac{\pi }{2},1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(\frac{\pi }{2},1) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot 1)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot 1) \\  & =2\cdot 1-0 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-f(\frac{\pi }{2},1) & ={f}_{y}(\frac{\pi }{2},1)(y-1) \\ z-0 & =2(y-1) \\ z & =2y-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(\frac{\pi }{2},1,0)$ can be given as the intersection of two planes:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=\frac{\pi }{2} \\ z=2y-2\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that:

- For the plane $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨1,0,0⟩.$

- For the plane $z=2y-2$ (or $2y-z-2=0$), a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨0,2,-1⟩.$

Finally, to find a direction vector for the tangent line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} & =⟨1,0,0⟩\times ⟨0,2,-1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =j+2\,k \\  & =⟨0,1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a tangent vector to $C$ at $P$ is $⟨0,1,2⟩.$

Question 11
?

The curve C is the intersection of a surface S, defined by z=f(x,y), with the plane x=π2. Given that the point P(π2,1,0) lies on C, and that fy=2sin⁡(xy)−cos⁡(π2y), which of the following gives a tangent vector to C at P?

a
⟨0,1,2⟩
b
⟨0,2,3⟩
c
⟨0,2,−1⟩
d
⟨0,3,2⟩
e
⟨0,1,−3⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The curve C is the intersection of the surface with the plane x=π2. Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve C at the point P will be given by the partial derivative fy(π2,1).

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative fy(x,y) at (π2,1):

fy(π2,1)=2sin⁡(π2⋅1)−cos⁡(π2⋅1)=2⋅1−0=2

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

z−f(π2,1)=fy(π2,1)(y−1)z−0=2(y−1)z=2y−2

Therefore, the tangent line to the curve C at P(π2,1,0) can be given as the intersection of two planes: {x=π2z=2y−2

Next, notice that:

  • For the plane x=π2, a normal vector to the plane is n1=⟨1,0,0⟩.

  • For the plane z=2y−2 (or 2y−z−2=0), a normal vector to the plane is n2=⟨0,2,−1⟩.

Finally, to find a direction vector for the tangent line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

n1×n2=⟨1,0,0⟩×⟨0,2,−1⟩=ijk10002−1=j+2k=⟨0,1,2⟩

Therefore, a tangent vector to C at P is ⟨0,1,2⟩.
